subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: finding an ally in the group [Action]
passage: After the temple fair, seven of them stood at the foot of the old water tower. "First one up the ladder gets a laddoo," said Suresh, rubbing his hands. Minakshi looked at the rusted rungs and her mouth went dry. Madhuri stood next to her with arms folded tight. Under her breath, Minakshi said, "Are you okay with this?" Madhuri shook her head, eyes wide. "No. Are you?" "No." Two words, and Minakshi's shoulders dropped. "We're not going up," she said, louder this time. "We'll hold the bags." Suresh groaned. "Boring!" But Madhuri did not move and neither did Minakshi, and two of the others glanced at each other and began to drift back. They ended up eating laddoos on the temple steps.

qa.q: How many friends stood at the foot of the water tower?
qa.a: Seven of them stood at the foot of the old water tower.

qa.q: How did Minakshi feel when Madhuri said 'No. Are you?'
qa.a: Minakshi felt relieved, shown by her shoulders dropping, since she was no longer alone in the doubt. 😊

qa.q: What could Minakshi do if Madhuri had said she was fine with it, and why?
qa.a: Minakshi could still say no for herself, suggest something else, and walk away, since one clear no still helps others who are unsure.

qa.q: How might Madhuri have felt before Minakshi asked?
qa.a: Madhuri was probably tense and alone with the worry, as the tightly folded arms and wide eyes suggest.

grounding: By quietly asking one friend if she is comfortable, the student finds support, and two people declining together makes it far easier to say no than standing alone.
